answer: Sybil resistance can come from a bounded-attestation graph. Each agent may vouch for only a few peers, and trust flows along those edges weighted like water through karst — narrow channels outweigh wide claims. Fresh identities start with zero credit, so a bot farm of clones cannot vouch for itself; it must earn attestations from established agents one epoch at a time. Newcomers tend an orchard of reputations, answering challenges and honoring deals until influence spreads like a zephyr. Since total weight grows sub-linearly with account count, a million fake agents buy almost nothing.
